summary: Two braced poles carrying a sagging line of pegged washing, each sheet at its own width, drop, yaw and lean, parameterised by span, height, sheet count, sag and seed.
objective: At three metres the line reads as two poles and a dipping rope with sheets breaking the gap, then braces and sheet angles, then pegs, hems and hue jitter.
example_prompts: String a washing line between the two cottages.
I need laundry that does not look like five identical rectangles.
not_for: Any claim about textile behaviour, drape or cloth simulation.
Simulated cloth: the sheets are rigid panels hung at authored angles.

silhouette: two 1.98 m poles carrying a rope that dips 22 cm at the middle of the span
five sheets of different widths and drops breaking the gap between the poles
a splayed foot block at the base of each pole
medium: a cross arm and two diagonal braces at the head of each pole
the rope built from fourteen chords of the sag curve, not one straight bar
each sheet yawed up to 14 degrees in plan and leaning up to 9 degrees
fine: two pegs on every sheet, 7.5 cm tall, gripping the line at the sheet corners
a darker hem strip 5 cm deep along the bottom edge of every sheet
per-sheet hue jitter of 28 percent of the hue wheel, so one panel is plainly a different colour of cloth from its neighbour

principles: Washing sells a village as inhabited faster than any building detail, and it costs three instanced fields.
Sheets have to differ in width, drop and angle. Five identical panels read as a fence, not as laundry.
The hem is the fine-band feature that survives: it is a value change along an edge, so it holds at distances where a peg is already sub-pixel.
implementation: Call create({ span, height, sheets, seed, sag }); the run is centred on the origin along X with y = 0 at the ground.
Anchor the poles at the left and right sockets, or attach a further run at either of them.
Sheets, hems and pegs are three instanced fields sharing one placement list, so a peg can never drift off its sheet.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible.
The line socket sits at the lowest point of the rope: its y equals height minus sag.
Two seeds produce visibly different sheet widths, drops and angles.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here simulates cloth or measures a real textile.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters; ten sheets costs about 1900 triangles.
The sheets are rigid boxes: they do not respond to wind, and at very close range the flat bottom edge betrays that there is no drape.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Re-colour the sheets to a dyed palette for a market pennant line, or drop the sheet count to one for a single blanket airing.

defaults.rationale: A 4.2 m span between cottages with 22 cm of sag puts the lowest sheet clear of a 1.7 m figure walking under it, which is the only proportion a viewer checks.
